question.worked_solution:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
y = \ln(x+3)+6
$$

Then, we swap $x$ and $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+3)+6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+3)+6 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(y+3) & =x-6 \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+3)} & ={e}^{x-6} \\ y+3 & ={e}^{x-6} \\ y & ={e}^{x-6}-3\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is $f^{-1}(x) = e^{x-6}-3.$
